findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] --resume breaks a LIVE lock and can let two writers corrupt the ledger. The resume-only stale-lock break deletes any existing .batch-ledger.lock WITHOUT checking whether the holder process is still alive. Scenario: driver A is still running and holds the lock; driver B starts --resume, removes A's LIVE lock, acquires its own, skips A's already-written records, and appends the rest while A keeps appending too -> duplicate/corrupt ledger, and B may exit 0 before A appends later duplicates. Fix: the stale-lock break must check the holder PID liveness (read the lock's holder.json/pid; break ONLY if the process is dead). A live holder means a genuine concurrent driver -> precondition_failed, not a break.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. acquireLock() now stamps LOCK_DIR/holder.json{pid}; the resume-only lock break probes holder liveness (process.kill(pid,0)) and breaks ONLY a dead/missing holder — a LIVE holder records precondition_failed to the blocked-ledger and exits 3. selfcheck-m3 (H) confirms: --resume refuses to break a live lock (exit 3) and breaks it only after the holder dies (discriminating).

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] Truncated-tail repair can wrongly drop a VALID final record. repairTruncatedTail truncates the trailing line, but a genuinely complete final record whose line simply lacks a trailing newline (valid JSON, no newline at EOF) would be dropped -> that iterationId becomes a GAP on resume (or a spurious re-run/dup). Fix: only drop the trailing segment if it does NOT parse as valid JSON (genuinely incomplete); if the last line parses cleanly, KEEP it as a complete record. Distinguish 'valid record, no trailing newline' (keep) from 'truncated partial write' (drop).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. repairTruncatedTail now parses the un-terminated tail in BOTH branches (shared isCompleteLedgerRecordLine helper): a complete final record missing only its trailing newline is PRESERVED verbatim; only a genuinely-incomplete partial write is dropped. selfcheck-m3 (G) confirms replay/small/4 preserved -> no gap.

findings.desc: repairTruncatedTail (run-batch.mjs:182-220) unconditionally drops everything after the last newline when the ledger file does not end with \n, even when that trailing fragment is a COMPLETE, valid, parseable JSON record — contradicting its own documented invariant ("Every COMPLETE prior record is preserved verbatim", line 178; "All well-formed prior lines are honored", line 129-131). Reproduced: a ledger of rec1\n + rec2 (rec2 complete JSON, only missing the trailing newline) has rec2 silently deleted by repairTruncatedTail, so its already-completed iteration is silently discarded and re-run on resume. The single-line branch (lastNl < 0, lines 197-209) DOES check JSON.parse before dropping and preserves a parseable lone line, but the multi-line branch (lines 210-219) drops unconditionally without ever checking whether the trailing fragment parses — an inconsistent/incomplete repair that can discard real evidence though it does not create a duplicate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055 (same fix as F-002 — the truncated-tail bug). Both single-line and multi-line branches now check parseability before dropping; a valid complete final record without a trailing newline is never dropped into a gap. selfcheck-m3 (G) covers it.

findings.desc: CHK-002 and understanding.json explicitly specify the H3 mid-iteration kill mechanism as the pre-existing POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT hook (a caught throw AFTER workspace write producing a verify_crash STOP record) — understanding.json facts: the mid-iteration crash hook already exists: POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT; unknowns: whether a mid-append truncated line actually occurs under POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT, resolved by the probe run. The delivered resume-probe.mjs (killA/killB, lines 339-345) and selfcheck-m3.mjs (killResumeTrial A/B, lines 350-352) never exercise POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT at all: both scored kills use the NEW POS_CRASH_BEFORE_APPEND_AT hard-exit hook at two different indices, i.e. the SAME mechanism twice, not two distinct injection points. The only real SIGKILL trial (externalSigkillTrial) is explicitly informational/non-gating and excluded from the dupTotal/gapTotal pass-fail computation. As a result resume behavior when the interrupted iteration already produced a caught stop record (rather than being genuinely recordless) is never asserted anywhere in M3 tests — the storys own pre-DEV automated advisory review (review.json unresolved_unknowns) flagged this exact unknown, and the implementation routed around it with a different mechanism rather than resolving it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. resume-probe.mjs killC uses POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT (a caught fault -> a recorded verify_crash STOP at replay/small/3), then resume SKIPS that already-recorded stop (stoppedRecordPreserved:true, not re-run into a proof); selfcheck-m3 sub-check F asserts the stop-record-resume path. The POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT mechanism is now exercised.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2 re-check, verified] --resume can STILL break a LIVE lock during the mkdir-to-holder stamp race. The F-001 fix stamps holder.json{pid} AFTER mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR), and the resume break treats a missing/malformed holder.json as stale. Scenario: driver A wins mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR) but has not yet completed writeFileSync(holder.json); driver B (--resume) sees LOCK_DIR with no/half-written holder.json, judges it stale, removes it, acquires its own, and both append concurrently -> corruption. The holder stamp is not an atomic part of lock acquisition. Fix: treat a MISSING/malformed/unparseable holder.json as LIVE (conservative — do NOT break; precondition_failed); break ONLY when holder.json exists with a parseable pid that is DEAD. A genuinely-orphaned prior run wrote holder.json before crashing so it stays breakable; only a crash in the tiny mkdir->stamp window is not auto-broken (safe: requires manual cleanup, never corruption). Add a selfcheck sub-check: a lock dir with NO holder.json is NOT broken by --resume.

Independently corroborating open F-005 (codex-host-2): isLockHolderAlive() (run-batch.mjs:325-341) treats a missing/unparseable holder.json as STALE (line 331: "missing / unreadable / malformed holder -> treat as stale"), and acquireLock() (run-batch.mjs) writes HOLDER_PATH only AFTER mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR) succeeds -- there is a real window between mkdir winning the lock and the holder.json write landing where a concurrent --resume run would see LOCK_DIR present with no holder.json, judge it stale, and rmSync it out from under a live driver, letting two writers append concurrently (ledger corruption). Confirmed by direct code read; the fix (conservative direction: missing/malformed holder.json should be treated as LIVE/unbreakable, not stale) is not yet present in this diff. This is the same root cause as F-005 and blocks a clean pass on the F-001 area of this round.

multi-resumer-toctou: run-batch.mjs:749-787 evaluateLockForBreak() computes a breakable/proven-dead verdict from a one-time read of holder.json, but the subsequent rmSync(LOCK_DIR) at line 780 is unconditional on path and never re-validates that the lock dir still holds the SAME dead-pid holder it evaluated. Concrete interleaving: two concurrent --resume drivers A and B both see the same genuinely-dead-pid holder.json and both compute {breakable:true}. A calls rmSync(LOCK_DIR) then acquireLock() -> mkdirSync succeeds -> A now owns a freshly-live lock (about to stamp its own holder.json). B, acting on its stale verdict computed before A re-acquired, calls rmSync(LOCK_DIR) unconditionally -> deletes A live lock -> B then calls acquireLock() -> mkdirSync succeeds -> both A and B hold non-null releasers and both proceed to appendRecord() to the SAME batch-ledger.jsonl concurrently. This reintroduces the exact two-writer ledger-corruption scenario the F-001/F-005/F-006 fix chain was built to prevent -- it is just triggered by a THIRD racing resumer rather than the single acquire-window case this round closed. selfcheck-m3.mjs has no sub-check exercising two concurrent --resume invocations (checks H and I are both single-resumer only), so this gap is untested. A fix needs either a fencing/generation check (re-read+compare holder.json immediately before rmSync, or a rename-based conditional delete) so a stale verdict can never delete a lock dir that has since been re-acquired by someone else.
